# Security Checklist: Getnet Assist Orchestration

**Purpose**: Validate that the security requirements for customer-data isolation, operator exposure, grounded answers, and container/runtime safety are complete, clear, and testable before release
**Created**: 2026-11-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` workflow based on the feature spec, plan, and constitution (Principles I, II, and V).
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Customer Data Isolation (Per-User Scoping)

- [ ] CHK001 Every account read (merchant profile, receivables, terminal state) is explicitly required to be scoped to the `user_id` on the request, never to an identifier taken from the message text (FR-006, Constitution II)
- [ ] CHK002 The spec defines the expected outcome when the request `user_id` has no record: an answered "not found" reply that discloses no other customer's data and does not escalate into another user's record
- [ ] CHK003 Cross-customer success is measurable: the evaluation run requires 0 replies disclosing another customer's profile, receivables, or machine state (SC-002)
- [ ] CHK004 Requirements state that a `user_id` embedded in the message body (e.g. "show me cliente9999's balance") must be ignored in favour of the authenticated request `user_id`

## Operator Exposure (Review Records and Logs)

- [ ] CHK005 Review records are explicitly prohibited from storing raw customer payloads, merchant legal names, amounts, or account numbers; only `user_id`, `trace_id`, route, tool names, source titles/URLs, retrieval scores, and latency may be stored (FR-013, data-model constraint)
- [ ] CHK006 Log requirements state that log lines carry only `user_id` and `trace_id` and never raw merchant payloads (Constitution II)
- [ ] CHK007 The trace endpoint requirement limits access to a single record by `trace_id` and defines the response for an unknown or malformed `trace_id` (404, no record data leaked)

## Grounded Answers (No Invented Facts)

- [ ] CHK008 Every product or policy reply is required to cite the public Getnet material used, or explicitly state that the material does not support an answer (FR-003, Constitution I)
- [ ] CHK009 The prohibition on inventing fees, settlement deadlines, product limits, or eligibility is stated as a hard requirement with a measurable zero-invention criterion (FR-004, SC-003)
- [ ] CHK010 The minimum retrieval score and the relative cut-off that trigger an "insufficient sources" handoff are defined, so a weak-match answer cannot be presented as grounded
- [ ] CHK011 General public lookup (weather, exchange rates) is required to return an empty Getnet source list and must never be used as evidence for Getnet product or policy claims (FR-008, SC-004)
- [ ] CHK012 When no model key is configured, the extractive fallback is required to return only retrieved passages with their titles and URLs, so no ungrounded text can be generated offline

## Guardrail, Refusal, and Input Validation

- [ ] CHK013 Refusal requirements cover instruction override (prompt injection), requests for another customer's data, and unsupported topics, with a measurable 0-leaked-facts criterion (FR-009, SC-006)
- [ ] CHK014 Empty messages and missing or malformed `user_id` values are rejected before any specialist or tool runs (FR-016, `ChatRequest` validation in data-model.md)
- [ ] CHK015 Human handoff requirements define the reference format and the closed set of reasons (`human_requested`, `low_confidence`, `insufficient_sources`), so escalation cannot be used to bypass a refusal

## Secrets, Configuration, and Container/Runtime Security

- [ ] CHK016 API keys and tokens (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`) are required to come only from environment variables; no secret value may be committed to the repository (`.env.example` ships empty, `.cursor/mcp.json` uses `${env:GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}`)
- [ ] CHK017 The packaged service is required to run as a single container exposing only port 8000 and only the two routes `POST /v1/chat` and `GET /v1/traces/{trace_id}` — no health, login, crawl, or dashboard surface (Constitution IV and V)
- [ ] CHK018 Container requirements are explicit about the runtime user and filesystem: whether the process must run as a non-root user and whether the corpus and fixture data are read-only at runtime are stated, not left implicit in the Dockerfile
- [ ] CHK019 Network egress requirements are bounded: corpus ingestion fetches only the two specified Getnet URLs, web lookup calls only the documented weather/exchange providers, and failure of any of them degrades to the on-disk corpus or an unavailable statement instead of failing open
- [ ] CHK020 Requirements state that the service must answer the evaluation set with no paid language service configured, so a missing or invalid `OPENAI_API_KEY` never changes the security posture (offline BM25 path, Constitution III and IV)

## Notes

- Items are unchecked on creation; checkbox state belongs to the reviewer and is not modified by `/speckit-implement`.
- Items marked complete refer to requirements quality, not implementation. Implementation evidence lives in `tests/test_guardrail.py`, `tests/test_contract.py`, and `tests/test_evaluation.py`.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline; link to relevant resources or documentation.
- Items are numbered sequentially (CHK001-CHK020) for easy reference.
